verdict.rationale: Twilio's Authy docs claim the app is "available for iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, and Linux," and one user describes the desktop app as having kept them from being locked out. Multiple community reports concretely contradict this: they say the desktop apps were EOL'd with near-immediate deprecation and that users had to move off when the macOS app's end of life was announced. The current features page also lists only iOS and Android, and the stop-gap of running the iPad app on Apple silicon Macs is described as not first-class. missing for 10: a currently supported first-party desktop app, vault/sync access on desktop, and current documentation of desktop surfaces.

support.subject: As a power user, a first-class desktop app gives me codes and vault access on my computer, not just on mobile

citations.quote: It's available for iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, and Linux.
the desktop app has more than once prevented them being locked out of a service
